method: Three agents simulated a beginner, a returning learner and an A2 learner with a short phone session. They inspected the built app in owned Chromium contexts with synthetic progress. Findings are reproducible product observations, not real-learner outcomes.

repairs.before: A failed scheduled recall followed by reload and a correct retry displayed independent recall despite the saved first failure.
repairs.after: Feedback consults today's saved first outcome; corrected work stays supported and unscheduled extra practice stays labelled separately. Dates and first attempts are not overwritten.

repairs.before: The ottimo transformation rejected 'Questa è una soluzione ottima.' despite the prompt allowing that position.
repairs.after: Both valid adjective positions are accepted in the existing exercise. Its ID and earlier recorded attempts are unchanged.

repairs.before: A diagnostic practice link could reopen a completed unit's old production instead of practice.
repairs.after: The explicit practice link opens the practice stage and uses due recall when eligible. Normal unit reopening retains its saved position; old production and attempts remain intact.

repairs.before: A new A1 learner with no dated evidence received an A2 chapter-check recommendation and an optional scheduled copy of that suggestion.
repairs.after: The no-specific-evidence fallback opens Today and the existing saved plan. Actual due reviews and specific topic catch-up retain priority; A2 checks remain available by choice.

repairs.before: A six-button stage list placed the first session input well below the initial phone screen.
repairs.after: Phone entry focuses and scrolls to the current activity using the existing cancellable navigation helper, without modifying drafts or stages. Desktop entry remains unchanged.

repairs.before: Tapping the already-selected listening mode cleared the response, transcript reveal and self-checks.
repairs.after: Selected-mode taps preserve the task; changing modes still starts the different task.

learningImprovement: Private listening contains an optional collapsed bilingual routine: predict, listen for gist, replay an uncertain detail, compare with text, then retell with a changed detail. This uses the existing tab-local response field and adds no score, upload or proficiency claim.
preserved: Stable lesson/exercise IDs, existing first attempts, writing, active programmes and version-one backups
Existing review schedules and the distinction between correction and later-day recall
Private source archives, connected documents and audio stay outside the public release
The shared authenticated browser and real learner storage are untouched

nextImprovementsToEvaluate.idea: A short optional listening/speaking session path within an explicitly selected time budget.
nextImprovementsToEvaluate.reason: The existing ten-minute daily layout omits separate input and speaking stages. The optional listening routine helps, but the planner was deliberately preserved in this repair.
nextImprovementsToEvaluate.validationNeeded: Observe whether learners can find and finish it without adding an unwanted second session; preserve ongoing session durations and credit.

nextImprovementsToEvaluate.idea: Additional unfamiliar prompts for delayed transfer and focused contrasts between confusable forms.
nextImprovementsToEvaluate.reason: Success on repeated quiz items is limited evidence for using Italian in a changed situation. Interleaving effects depend on task and outcome.
nextImprovementsToEvaluate.validationNeeded: Teacher review of original prompts, then later-day performance on unpractised details; do not use XP as an outcome measure.

nextImprovementsToEvaluate.idea: A small real-learner evaluation with teacher or conversation-partner feedback.
nextImprovementsToEvaluate.reason: Agent simulations find interface and scoring defects but cannot establish comprehension, retention or conversational improvement.
nextImprovementsToEvaluate.validationNeeded: Voluntary feedback and a simple later-day recall/short conversation task, with support use recorded separately and no unrequested analytics collection.

limits: A targeted audit, not a complete accessibility review or systematic literature review. Browser tests do not assess teaching effectiveness, spontaneous speaking or device-voice quality.
